process: U.S. distillery energy intensity, Jacques et al. 2003 (Ch.2, p.5)

value: Distillery using continuous column-still distillation (column stills operated continuously; lower energy intensity than pot stills).

note: Column-still distilleries, printed 10 to 29 kBtu/gallon (80 proof). Total energy use (all carriers) printed in kBtu/gallon (80 proof); converted to MJ per litre of pure alcohol: x1.055056/3.785412 then /0.4 (80 proof = 40% alcohol; the source itself equates 70-75 kBtu/gal 200 proof with 28-30 kBtu/gal 80 proof). heating-value basis not stated. reprinted from BIER (2012). Same sample restated as 2.8-8.0 MJ/liter (80 proof) on p.103 and p.137, see other-values.

value: Distillery using batch pot-still distillation (pot stills operated in batch mode; typically higher energy intensity than column stills).

note: Pot-still distilleries, printed between 29 and 110 kBtu/gallon (80 proof). Same sample restated as 8.0-30.8 MJ/liter (80 proof) on p.103 and p.137.

value: Integrated beverage-spirits distillery, average of the international benchmark sample.

note: Average total energy use of the sample, printed 34.4 kBtu/gallon (80 proof). commercial

value: Mechanical vapor recompression: a centrifugal fan or compressor raises the pressure and temperature of vapour leaving the still so its heat can be reused (still heating, wash/mash preheat, hot water, pot-ale evaporators).

note: With MVR, still condensers can be designed to produce hot water at temperatures up to 185 degF (85 degC).

value: commercial
note: Piloted 2002 at Sungrain Chita (Japan); used at Jameson Midleton (2014) and Chivas Strathclyde.

process: Jameson Midleton distillery expansion (Ch.13 case studies, p.108, p.111)

note: For each pound of water removed approximately 1,350 Btu are needed; per t of water evaporated; Btu/lb converted to GJ/t. Carrier fuel or steam (unspecified). heating-value basis not stated. reprinted from Jacques et al. (2003)

value: Low-temperature belt dryer: spent grain on perforated plates carried through the dryer while air at 70-90 degC is pulled through it; can use waste heat from cooking, mashing and distillation.

process: Low-temperature belt drying of spent grains (Ch.15, p.126)
note: Needs about 1 kWh of heat to remove 1 kg of water; per t of water removed (1 kWh/kg = 3.6 GJ/t). Feed about 15% dry matter dried to about 70-80%. heating-value basis not stated.

process: Low-temperature belt drying of spent grains (Ch.15, p.126)
note: Uses a temperature of about 158-194 degF (70-90 degC).

value: Single-effect evaporator concentrating thin stillage: a calandria heats the liquor to boiling, a separator splits off the vapour and a condenser rejects its heat.

note: The efficiency of a simple evaporator system results in about one unit of steam removing one unit of water; t steam per t water evaporated. heating-value basis not applicable. reprinted from Monceaux and Kuehner (2009)

value: Electric boiler using resistance heating (electrode, induction or infrared also possible) to raise hot water or steam.

note: Electric boilers are highly efficient, often reaching 95% efficiency. heating-value basis not applicable.

Lifetimes of at least 15 years.

value: Electrode boiler passing current through the water, producing hot water or (superheated) steam.

note: Electrode boilers can have capacities up to 70 MWe (electric-input). CAPACITY BASIS: electric-input (the note gives electric input; basis read back 2026-10-02).
Producing hot water or (superheated) steam up to 660 degF (350 degC).

note: Electric efficiencies for simple cycle gas turbines can approach 40% high heating value; efficiency degrades quickly at part load. HHV.
